name: The Vancura Position
summary: The Vancura Position is the key drawing method in rook and rook's pawn versus rook: the defending rook attacks the pawn from the side and gives flank checks.
intro: The Vancura Position, also known as the Vancura Defense, is the essential drawing method in the endgame of rook and one pawn versus rook when the pawn is a rook's pawn. Named after Josef Vancura, it shows the defender holding a draw not by passive resistance but by activity: the rook attacks the pawn from the side along the sixth rank, ready to check the enemy king the moment it approaches, while the defending king sits safely near the corner.
boardCaption: Black to move: with the white king on g2, rook on a8, and pawn on a6 against the black king on h7 and rook on f6, the defending rook attacks the a-pawn from the side along the sixth rank, the heart of the Vancura draw.

sections.heading: The Drawing Setup
paragraphs: Everything in the Vancura Position depends on the pawn still standing on the sixth rank. With the pawn on a6 rather than a7, Black's rook on f6 attacks it from the side while remaining fully active. The rook cannot simply capture the pawn, because White's rook on a8 defends it, but that is not the point: by tying White's rook to the pawn's defense, the sideways attack freezes White's whole position.

The second pillar of the setup is the defending king. Black's king stays quietly on h7, safe near the corner and out of the way of checks and rook maneuvers. From the sixth rank the black rook does double duty: it bears down on the a6-pawn and stands perfectly placed to check the white king from the flank if it ever tries to march up the board to shelter its pawn.

sections.heading: Side Checks in Action
paragraphs: The mechanism is best seen in motion. After 1...Rg6+ 2.Kf2 Rf6+ 3.Ke2 Rg6, the black rook simply swings back and forth along the sixth rank. Whenever the white king comes near, a check from the side drives it away; as soon as the checks pause, the rook returns to bear down on the a-pawn. Black repeats this pattern indefinitely, and White can find no way through.

This is why White can make no progress. The winning plan would be to bring the king across to support the pawn and free the rook from its defensive post on a8, but the moment the king tries to shelter in front of its pawn, a flank check drives it away again. The pawn cannot safely advance, the rook cannot leave it, and the game is a draw.

sections.heading: Why Activity Draws
paragraphs: The Vancura Defense embodies the great principle of rook endgames: the active rook draws, the passive rook loses. The losing method in this ending is to let the defending rook sit passively in front of the pawn or directly behind it, where it does nothing but blockade. The Vancura rook, by contrast, works from the side, combining an attack on the pawn with the constant threat of flank checks.

Timing matters as much as placement. The defense works while the pawn is still on the sixth rank, which is exactly what allows the rook to strike at it laterally along that rank while staying mobile. Defenders in rook and rook's pawn versus rook should therefore aim for this setup deliberately: rook to the sixth rank attacking the pawn from the side, king tucked safely in the corner, checks ready whenever the enemy king advances.

keyIdeas: The Vancura Position is the standard draw in rook and rook's pawn versus rook while the pawn is still on the sixth rank.
The defending rook attacks the pawn from the side along the sixth rank, staying active rather than blockading.
Flank checks drive the attacking king away whenever it tries to shelter in front of its pawn.
The defender does not grab the pawn, since the attacker's rook defends it; the sideways pressure alone ties White down.
The defending king belongs safely near the corner, on squares like h7 and g7.
An active rook draws this ending; a rook sitting passively in front of or behind the pawn loses.

white: Free the rook from defending the pawn so the pawn can advance.
March the king toward the pawn to shelter and support it.
Push the pawn forward if the defender's pressure ever lapses.
black: Attack the pawn from the side along the sixth rank.
Give flank checks whenever the white king approaches the pawn.
Keep the king safe near the corner on h7 and g7.
